record: Operational settings for the conference paper (fast-track). Written 2026-11-07 BEFORE any T-a result on P1 and BEFORE any P2 scoring. P1-only operational reasoning; no P2 score, label or outcome used.
status: PROPOSED_FOR_FREEZE (owner approval freezes this exact file by its SHA-256)

ta_primary.name: Recall-at-relative-quota
ta_primary.selection: hard cap (A1b.1): rank by (score desc, A1.2 tie key asc); alert whole indistinguishable groups only while they fit; first non-fitting group omitted, no backfill
ta_primary.tie_key: A1.2: first 8 bytes LE uint64 of SHA-256(seed 20261104 LE8 || a_i int64 us LE8 || raw parsed float64 72-feature vector in frozen schema order)
ta_primary.batches: hourly, membership by availability time a = Timestamp + Flow Duration (T2), UTC hour floor(a / 1 h), per capture file; hours never cross capture files
ta_primary.decision_time: D_h = max(C_h, max a_s) = end of hour h (delta_score = 0); reported as a retrospective batch policy only
ta_primary.recall: flow-level pooled Sigma TP_h / Sigma K_h per day; time-block sensitivity = unweighted mean over attack-containing hours; day without attacks -> undefined
ta_primary.days: attack-containing days only (P1 Tue-Fri; P2 both days). Never used for Monday FPR or model selection

analyst_review_capacity.R: not modelled; assumption R = k_h (every alert issued inside the quota is reviewed). Stated in the paper as an assumption

annotation_budget.role: labels obtained per hour for ESTIMATING detector performance (audit sample drawn from all completed flows of the hour, alerted or not); never used to train, adapt or threshold the detector
annotation_budget.design: M0 only: stratified SRSWOR by hour, b_h = min(b, N_h); M1/M2 alert-stratified designs deferred
annotation_budget.estimators: per-day recall and FPR of the fixed detector under T-b (alpha 0.01) and under T-a primary: combined ratio estimator over hourly strata with weights N_h / b_h; 95% CI by Taylor linearisation with finite-population correction (Cochran 1977, stratified ratio estimator)
annotation_budget.reported: bias vs census, empirical CI coverage, mean CI width, P(zero audited attack flows) per day, audited attack flows and attack-containing hours with every result

rationale.q_0.01: Equal to the primary nominal FPR alpha = 0.01, so the T-a quota and the T-b threshold target the same nominal alert fraction; their comparison then isolates threshold transfer (T-b) from ranking under a fixed volume (T-a). On P1 hourly batches (N_h ~ 0.7k-59k flows) it gives at most ~590 alerts per hour, inside the 100-2000 absolute-capacity range proposed in A1b.2.
rationale.K_500: Middle value of the A1b.2 candidate set {100, 500, 2000}. Volume-independent: tests whether conclusions survive when the alert budget does not scale with traffic, which matters for cross-testbed data whose hourly volume differs from P1 (known only as aggregate counts from the Stage 02A-0 feasibility audit, not tuned on).
rationale.one_sensitivity_only: Fast-track scope: the contrast relative vs absolute budget is the scientifically informative one; further values are deferred.

change_rule: Any change needs a new versioned record written before the affected evaluation.
